newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas holds in Gulf, slips in West.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas holds in Gulf, slips in West.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices on the Gulf Coast pipes remained strong Thursday despite forecasts for cooler weather in the Northeast and central U.S., industry sources said.
Swing prices on the Gulf pipes held in the low-to-mid $1.80s per million British thermal units as storage buying escalated.

Despite the firmness in the Gulf, prices out West eased as news of El Paso's return to partial service surfaced. Traders reported closing Permian basin deals in the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s, down more than five cents from Wednesday.

El Paso Natural Gas reported earlier today that it has completed repairs to one of the two pipes damaged last Tuesday, returning about 480 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas to the market. The company could not comment on when the second line would return to service. A total of 550 mmcfd had been removed by the outage.
Prices at Waha were equally weaker due to the ample supply. Traders reported closing deals in the mid-$1.60s to low-$1.70s.

At the southern California border, gas sold in the low-to-mid $1.70s. The western third of the U.S. is expected to experience below-normal temperatures next week, which should put further pressure on the market in the near-term.

In the Midcontinent, prices edged only slightly lower to the mid-to-high $1.60s amid significantly cooler temperatures. Forecasters are calling for temperatures seven to 12 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal in the region through Sunday.
